claims.text: The target system is an equimolar multicomponent high-entropy alloy such as CoFeMnNiCr in solid and liquid states.
Conventional EAM references inadequately represent the range of atomic configurations present in the ab initio liquid.
The EAM reference should be replaced by a DNN or moment-tensor potential trained on ab initio solid and liquid configurations.
Active learning can construct a DNN training set from AIMD configurations of both crystalline and liquid states.
Training and validation will cover temperatures from 0.2 to 1.0 times the melting temperature.
The range from 0.2 to 1.0 times the melting temperature spans the onset of melting through fully developed liquid states.
A DNN potential implicitly encodes complex many-body correlations.
A DNN potential represents variability among local atomic configurations more faithfully than an EAM potential.
A DeepMD potential trained on DFT data can accurately describe both solid and liquid phases.
Training on diverse ab initio configurations enables accurate mapping of energies over a broad configurational range.
Training on diverse ab initio configurations enables accurate mapping of atomic forces over a broad configurational range.
The DNN reference will improve reference–target phase-space overlap relative to EAM references.
Improved reference–target phase-space overlap will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
The DNN reference will reduce TI path mismatch by approximately 40–50% relative to TOR-TILD EAM references.
The resulting free-energy differences will be within approximately 5 meV/atom of direct ab initio integration benchmarks.
The proposed improvement depends on the training set adequately covering both solid and liquid configurations.
Under-sampling rare or transitional configurations near melting may prevent the DNN from reducing TI path mismatch.
Direct ab initio integration can serve as the decisive free-energy benchmark for comparing DNN and EAM references.

contradictions.description: The material and boundary fields restrict the hypothesis to temperatures near high melting temperatures, whereas the stated training and validation range extends down to 0.2 Tm, which is not ordinarily a near-melting condition.
